the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: Since s is locally of finite presentation the fibre F_u is locally of finite type over kappa(u), so dim_{e(u)}(F_u) is finite and the proof argues by induction on it. If dim_{e(u)}(F_u) equals dim(G_u) there is nothing to prove. Otherwise the slice lemma applies and produces an immersion g : U' to U with properties (1), (2), (3), a strict dimension drop dim_{e(u)}(F'_u) < dim_{e(u)}(F_u) in place of (6), and h = s composed with pr_1 Cohen-Macaulay only at the point (u, e(u)) in place of (4) and (5). The local source remark yields the largest open U'' of U' on which h is Cohen-Macaulay, which contains (u, e(u)) and hence u, and after replacing U' by U'' the morphism h is Cohen-Macaulay everywhere; the restrict-property lemma, together with base change of locally finite presentation morphisms and base change of Cohen-Macaulay morphisms, then shows s' and t' are locally of finite presentation and Cohen-Macaulay. The dimension has dropped, so the induction hypothesis applies to the restricted groupoid at the point u, which is still a finite type point of U' by the identification of finite type points. The solution g' : U'' to U' of the restricted problem composes with g to a map g'' = g composed with g' which solves the original problem: properties (1), (2), (3), (5) and (6) are immediate, and (4) holds because h'' is locally of finite presentation and Cohen-Macaulay by the double restrict-property lemma, using that Cohen-Macaulay morphisms are fppf local on the target. (source lines 2268-2323)
